q: Efficiency is another technical term that is derived from ____.
e: Though common in speech, efficiency has a precise scientific meaning.

q: In physics and engineering, efficiency has a ____.
e: It is quantitatively defined as a ratio of useful output to total input.

q: A simple machine is a mechanical device that amplifies the magnitude of a force and ____.
e: Simple machines redirect or magnify applied forces.

q: Simple machines are used to make ____ easier.
e: They reduce the effort needed to perform tasks.

q: Nowadays, machines are just combinations or more complicated forms of the ____ simple machines.
e: All complex machines derive from these basic types.

q: The six simple machines are lever, wheel and axle, pulley, inclined plane, screw and ____.
e: These are the foundational mechanical devices.
It is the ratio of load overcome to effort applied.

q: In practice, friction is always present. It should, therefore, be remembered that some effort is spent in overcoming ____.
e: Friction reduces the effective output of real machines.

q: The ratio of the distance moved by the effort to that of the load in the same time is called the ____ of the machine.
e: Velocity ratio relates input and output displacements.
It compares how far the effort moves versus the load.

q: The work obtained is called the ____ work.
e: This is the useful work delivered by the machine.

q: The work supplied is called the ____ work.
e: This is the total work put into the machine.

q: The ratio of output work to input work is defined as the ____ of the machine.
e: Efficiency measures how well a machine converts input to useful output.

q: Efficiency is generally expressed in the ____ form.
e: It is commonly given as a percent to indicate performance.
This converts the ratio into a percentage value.
This formula links efficiency to mechanical advantage and velocity ratio.

q: It is impossible, in practice, to build a perfect machine for which output work is equal to ____ work.
e: Real machines always lose some energy, usually to friction.

q: Therefore, the efficiency of a machine must always be less than ____.
e: No real machine can be perfectly efficient.
